title: Fallout
provenance: Reported by udance4ever (highball-db#862, 2026-11-01), Apple M1, macOS 27.2, Highball 0.10.23, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, D3DMetal, rated 2 of 5 after 1 minutes: the opening logo plays at 120 fps and then slows to a crawl, the same with every graphics mode and all four of its launch options, the GOG copy. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#862 (2026-11-03), in a Wine 11 environment on engine x64-crossover26.3-r28: on DXVK the logo still slows down. On D3DMetal and DXMT it slows down too and the window doesn't come up at the right size, and on WineD3D the game hangs, where on the Wine 10 engine it ran. The run was meant to try athei's x87sidecar, but the log has no sidecar attach line, so the sidecar wasn't active. udance4ever again on highball-db#862 (2026-11-04) tried FunkyFr3sh's cnc-ddraw with ddraw=n,b, without saying yet whether the logo still slows down. Those runs' logs show Wine's fixme lines, so the environment's WINEDEBUG reached Wine and replaced Highball's default, but no DLL load lines, which fits the quoted value " loaddll” seen in the same environment the next day (highball-db#993): Wine reads it as a channel name that doesn't exist. Highball 0.10.25 removes a ROSETTA_X87_PATH set by hand and sets it only itself, when the environment has HB_X87SIDECAR=1 and its engine ships the sidecar (the Wine 11 engines r30 and r31, Highball 0.10.26), so a hand-set path never reaches Wine there. That, not the variable's spelling, is why the sidecar never attached in the 2026-11-03 run. udance4ever again on highball-db#862 (2026-11-06), the Wine 11 engine r30 with athei's x87sidecar switched on (HB_X87SIDECAR=1 in the environment's variables, Highball 0.10.26): the sidecar attached to falloutwHR.exe (its line is in the log). The opening logo now starts at normal speed but still slows to a crawl if left to run. Clicking past it reaches the title menu, character creation and the game, which crawls again at the Overseer's talking head. The same in DXMT and WineD3D mode. In both logs DDRAW.dll from the game's folder loads as builtin, right after wined3d, so Wine's own ddraw ran, not cnc-ddraw (no ddraw override in that run's DLL overrides), and the GOG copy's high resolution patch (f1_res.dll) loads d3d9 and d3dx9_31, so the game drew through Direct3D 9, which goes through WineD3D in both modes.
notes: Doesn't play well yet in one report on an M1, the GOG copy. On the Wine 11 engine r30 with athei's x87sidecar on, it gets in game, but the opening logo and the talking heads slow to a crawl. The GOG copy's high resolution patch draws through Direct3D 9. Fallout Community Edition (github.com/alexbatalov/fallout1-ce), an open source rebuild of the engine, has a native Mac app that uses the game's own data files. It's a 32-bit game.

knownIssues.symptom: Slows to a crawl a moment into the opening logo, with every graphics mode (M1, Wine 10 r28 and Wine 11 r28). On Wine 11 r30 with the x87 sidecar the logo starts at normal speed and the game can be reached, but it crawls again later, at the Overseer's talking head
knownIssues.fix: none known. The x87 sidecar on r30 helps at the start but not further in (highball-db#862, 2026-11-06). Untested: DXVK mode on r30 with the sidecar, so that the patch's Direct3D 9 goes through DXVK instead of WineD3D. cnc-ddraw only comes into play with ddraw=n,b in the DLL overrides, and the high resolution patch draws through Direct3D 9 rather than DirectDraw
